input.quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 lets either Party stop the annual renewal on ninety (90) days' written notice, but it never says that exit is available without cause, so the Company's convenience right is only implicit; we make it express while keeping the notice period and the end-of-term structure that already suit us (HDI's right remains exercisable only against renewal, on 90 days' notice). The material fallback failure is the fee: Section 4.2(a) charges the Company a Termination Payment of one half of twelve months' Net Sales less $800,000 on any Company termination, uncapped and payable over eight quarters under 4.2(c), which far exceeds three months' fees. We therefore cap it at three months of the Section 3.1 payments. We target the fallback, not preferred: notice stays at 90 days rather than 30 and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, which we note but do not press. Separately (outside this rule) Section 4.2(a) also triggers the payment where the Company terminates for HDI's breach; that belongs under a cause/remedies rule.

proposal.summary: Make the Company's convenience right express and cap the Termination Payment at three months of fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made express that the Company may terminate for convenience and without cause on the existing ninety (90) days' notice against renewal, and we have capped the Section 4.2 Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees so that our exit is not penalised by an uncapped share of twelve months' Net Sales. This is our fallback position on convenience termination and early-termination fees.

ops.text: In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments due from the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.
